Subject: Re: Performance/SLO qualifications + customer-led load test (FinWise)

Thanks for the call earlier, Sara — good alignment overall. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same frame: 

What we heard (FinWise targets)
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for single-turn text generation (non-streamed).
- Throughput: sustained 150 req/s during peak windows; bursts to 300 req/s for up to 2 minutes.
- Concurrency: up to 100 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming: you do want streaming for partial results in the agent flows (chunked responses, client handles partials).

Planned customer-led load test (proposal)
- Window: Tue 2026-03-10, 10:00–13:00 PST (we can shift if you need a different slot).
- Script: you mentioned k6/Locust — we usually ship a k6 scenario that exercises streaming, KV-cache warmup, and typical prompt lengths.
- Success criteria: p95 < 200ms for non-streamed baseline; no errors > 1% sustained; memory/CPU on our dedicated pool not exceeding threshold (we'll monitor).

Next actions (owners)
- FinWise: confirm final test window and provide IPs that will originate traffic (Sara).
- Redwood (Logan): provide test account/API key, allowlist IPs, and k6 script.
- Redwood (Marissa/Aditya): be on the call to monitor metrics (latency p50/p95, errors, token throughput) and coordinate fallbacks.

Attachments we can provide: k6 script (k6_load_test_v2.js), brief runbook, and a temporary test API key.

If that looks good I will send the test credentials and allowlist ranges today so your infra can configure outbound rules.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123

Great — thanks for the quick reply, Sara. See below for the details we provisioned to support the test.

1) Test account / credentials (temporary)
- API key (test, expires 2026-03-17): redwood_test_FinWise_3m_abc123
- Scope: points to a dedicated staging pool with identical instance types to your expected production pool; token limits and quotas set for test window.

2) Allowlist/IPs for FinWise to allow inbound to our control-plane/test-collector (so we can validate traffic origin):
- 35.234.120.10/32
- 35.234.120.11/32

Note: those are our collector IPs; you should also allow outbound traffic from the egress IPs you listed (we will accept traffic from them).

3) Attached: k6_load_test_v2.js (k6 scenario that includes:
   - ramping to 150 req/s sustained with occasional 300 req/s bursts
   - streaming check that opens a streaming connection and validates chunk order and reconnect behavior
   - warmup sequence to populate KV cache for prefix hits)

4) Quick curl examples (non-streamed + streamed)
- Non-streamed: 
  curl -X POST https://api.staging.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer redwood_test_FinWise_3m_abc123" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-gen-1","input":"Summarize recent transactions for account 1234","max_tokens":150}'

- Streamed (chunked): 
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer redwood_test_FinWise_3m_abc123" 
    -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
    -X POST https://api.staging.redwoodinference.com/v1/stream 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-gen-1","input":"Real-time agent: provide partial suggestions as they become available","stream":true}'

5) Runbook/monitoring plan (we'll be on the call):
- Marissa will watch p95 latency, errors, CPU/GPU utilization, and token throughput.
- Aditya will have console access to adjust batch sizes or switch to a lower-capacity variant if we see memory pressure.
- We will collect and share k6 raw outputs, raw traces, and a short regression check against the last known baseline.

Attachments: k6_load_test_v2.js, loadtest-credentials.txt (contains the API key + expiry note).

If anything looks off (IP ranges, key expiry, script content) shout and we will update. Otherwise we'll lock the window for 2026-03-10 10:00–13:00 PST.

Thanks — Logan

Locking in — I will be on the call for monitoring. Quick internal checklist for the test run: 
- Dashboard: latency p50/p95, errors, token/s (dashboard link in our runbook).
- Tracing: enable request-level traces for the first 15 minutes to catch regressions.
- Fallback plan: if p95 > 350ms or errors > 3% sustained for 2 min, we shift FinWise to the lower-memory quantized variant (auto-failover) and pause the k6 script.
- Aditya: please prepare a short playbook to adjust batching and model variant; I'll coordinate the signal to pause/rollback.

See you both on 2026-03-10; I"ll send the monitoring link and dial-in in a calendar invite.

Marissa
